subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How many performances must a candidate present for Component 2: Performing?
options: One performance only
Two performances: one solo and one ensemble
Three performances of contrasting styles
Four performances, all as a soloist
questions.explain: Component 2 requires each candidate to give two performances, one as a soloist and one as a member of an ensemble.

questions.q: What best describes an ensemble performance in Component 2?
options: Performing an individual part together with one or more other performers
Performing entirely on your own with no other players
Conducting a group without playing an instrument
Playing a backing track through a speaker
questions.explain: An ensemble performance requires the candidate to play or sing their own part alongside at least one other live performer.

questions.q: In assessing a performance, 'accuracy' refers mainly to:
options: Playing the correct notes and rhythms
Choosing a fashionable piece of music
Wearing suitable concert clothing
Introducing the piece to the audience
questions.explain: Accuracy is judged principally on correct pitches and rhythms as written in the score.

questions.q: Which of these is an element of interpretation rather than accuracy?
options: Shaping dynamics and phrasing to communicate the music's character
Playing every note exactly as printed
Keeping strictly to the correct rhythmic values
Starting and finishing on the written pitches
questions.explain: Interpretation concerns expressive choices such as dynamics, phrasing and articulation, beyond simply playing the right notes.

questions.q: If a soloist is supported by a piano accompaniment, the accompaniment is:
options: Allowed, but only the candidate's own playing is assessed
Assessed equally alongside the soloist
Not permitted under any circumstances
Marked as a second ensemble performance
questions.explain: A soloist may be accompanied, but assessment focuses solely on the candidate's own performance.

questions.q: Why should a candidate's ensemble part be independent rather than doubled by another player throughout?
options: To demonstrate genuine ensemble skill rather than relying on another performer
To make the piece sound louder overall
Because doubling is impossible on most instruments
So the performance can be shorter
questions.explain: An independent part shows the candidate can hold their own line within a texture, which is the point of ensemble assessment.

questions.q: Two flute players perform a duet in which both flutes play exactly the same line in unison from start to finish. What is the likely problem for the ensemble mark?
options: The candidate's part is not independent, so it may not count as a genuine ensemble
The piece is too quiet to be heard
Flutes are not allowed in ensembles
The performance would be too long
questions.explain: Constant unison doubling gives no independent part, so it fails to show true ensemble skill.

questions.q: How are the two performances marked in Component 2?
options: Each performance is marked out of 30, giving a total of 60
Both are combined into a single mark out of 30
Only the stronger performance is marked
Each is marked out of 100
questions.explain: The solo and ensemble performances are each marked out of 30 for a combined total of 60.

questions.q: What best distinguishes accuracy from interpretation?
options: Accuracy is about correct notes and rhythms; interpretation is about expressive communication
Accuracy is about volume; interpretation is about speed
They mean exactly the same thing
Accuracy applies only to solos and interpretation only to ensembles
questions.explain: Accuracy concerns technical correctness while interpretation concerns musical expression and character.

questions.q: During an ensemble performance a candidate consistently rushes ahead and loses contact with the other players. Which skill most needs improvement?
options: Keeping in time and awareness of the other performers
Reading the treble clef
Choosing a louder instrument
Learning the correct fingering
questions.explain: Staying together relies on rhythmic control and listening to the ensemble, key aspects of ensemble awareness.

questions.q: Ensemble awareness in a performance includes:
options: Listening to others, keeping together and balancing your part
Playing as loudly as possible at all times
Ignoring the other performers to stay focused
Finishing before the other players
questions.explain: Good ensemble playing means listening, staying together rhythmically and balancing your sound within the group.

questions.q: Why should a candidate choose a piece of an appropriate level of difficulty?
options: The level of difficulty of the music is taken into account in the marking
Only easy pieces are permitted
Difficulty has no effect on the mark at all
Harder pieces are automatically given full marks
questions.explain: The demand of the chosen piece is considered, so a suitably challenging yet secure piece allows access to higher marks.

questions.q: How are Component 2 performances submitted for assessment?
options: They are recorded and the recordings are submitted for moderation
They are performed live to a visiting examiner from Cambridge
They are described in a written essay only
They are submitted as sheet music without any sound
questions.explain: Performances are recorded and the recordings, with documentation, are submitted for external moderation.

questions.q: Who initially marks a candidate's performances in Component 2?
options: The centre (teacher), with the marks externally moderated by Cambridge
An external examiner who alone decides the mark
The candidate marks their own performance
Another candidate in the class
questions.explain: Component 2 is internally assessed by the centre and then externally moderated by Cambridge.

questions.q: A candidate plays all the correct notes but the performance sounds flat and mechanical. Which change would most improve the interpretation mark?
options: Adding appropriate dynamics, phrasing and expression
Playing the piece much faster throughout
Repeating the piece a second time
Choosing an easier piece
questions.explain: Expressive shaping through dynamics and phrasing communicates the music's character and lifts the interpretation.

questions.q: Which pair are examples of articulation?
options: Staccato and legato
Forte and piano
Allegro and adagio
Major and minor
questions.explain: Staccato (detached) and legato (smooth) describe articulation, an important element of interpretation.

questions.q: What does good 'balance' mean in an ensemble performance?
options: Adjusting your volume so your part fits sensibly with the others
Always being the loudest player
Standing in the centre of the group
Playing exactly the same notes as everyone else
questions.explain: Balance means controlling your dynamic level so no part dominates unless the music requires it.

questions.q: An examiner notes: 'secure notes and rhythm, but little sense of light and shade.' Which area should the candidate work on?
options: Communication and interpretation, especially dynamic contrast
Learning the correct notes
Playing more quietly overall
Choosing a different instrument
questions.explain: 'Light and shade' refers to dynamic and expressive contrast, part of communication and interpretation.

questions.q: During an ensemble a candidate hears they are drifting out of time and adjusts to match the others. This demonstrates:
options: Responding to and staying with the ensemble
A lack of accuracy in the notes
Poor choice of repertoire
Strong solo technique only
questions.explain: Listening and adjusting to keep together is a core ensemble skill.

questions.q: Why is a soloist's piano accompaniment not included in the assessment?
options: Only the candidate's own performance is being assessed
Piano accompaniments are always played incorrectly
Accompaniments are marked in Component 3 instead
The accompanist is usually another candidate
questions.explain: The mark reflects the candidate's own playing, so the accompaniment supports but is not itself assessed.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Music (0410) syllabus; Component 2: Performing
